title: Fetch MCP Server
summary: Let your agent download a web page and read it as clean markdown, in chunks, using the reference fetch server from the MCP project.
description: The fetch server adds one tool, fetch, that takes a URL and returns the page as markdown. You can ask for a longer slice with max_length and start_index, or request the raw HTML.
It is a Python package started with uvx, so you need uv installed. There is no account and no key.
By default it refuses private and loopback addresses and obeys a site's robots.txt for requests the model makes, which keeps an agent from poking at your internal network.
useWhen: Read a documentation page you paste as a link
Summarize a long blog post or RFC in several chunks
Pull the text of a public issue or changelog into the chat
Compare two vendor pages without opening a browser

mcp.name: fetch
access: Makes outbound HTTP requests to any public URL the agent chooses
Blocks loopback and private addresses unless you add a flag

example.prompt: Fetch https://example.com/docs/migration and give me the steps in order.
example.result: The page came back as markdown in one chunk. Steps: 1. Update the config key. 2. Rename the two deprecated methods. 3. Run the codemod. 4. Rebuild. The page has a note that step 3 is optional.

faq.question: Why did a fetch fail with a robots.txt error?
faq.answer: The server checks robots.txt for model-initiated fetches and refuses when the site disallows it or the file cannot be reached. The flag --ignore-robots-txt turns the check off, so use it only for sites you own.

faq.question: Can I limit which sites it may visit?
faq.answer: Yes. Add --allowed-hosts followed by hostnames, such as docs.python.org or a wildcard like *.wikipedia.org, to the args.

faq.question: How do I read a very long page?
faq.answer: The default cap is 5000 characters per call. Ask the agent to call fetch again with a higher start_index to continue where it stopped.

access: Reads public web pages over the network
